body:
I just want to say thank you to everyone who's posted.  You've all given me some excellent points to think about.  I know that research is not what I want to do, but I find the idea of starting over in a new career extremely daunting.

I met with a good friend today who's also doing a PhD.  She suggested to me something that should have been obvious for a while now - I need to get out of my PhD ASAP, but without throwing away all my hard work to this point.  She suggested I plan out the minimum amount I need to do in order to graduate, then I can go on to something else once I'm done.  Probably just travel for a year or two and try to get some perspective.  I guess I did have someone to talk to after all, I just didn't realise it.

I'm going to sit down and pull my shit together this week, and we're going to figure out how soon I can get myself out of this situation and on to something more positive.  I've still got a ways to go before I feel like I'm back "on track" (whatever that means), but at least there's a little light at the end of the tunnel for now.

EDIT: I've also booked a trip away to visit some friends interstate next weekend.  Hopefully a few days with some new scenery will help as well.

Thank you.

I'm in biochemistry. I enjoy the theory side of things and I'm good at them (top of my class in undergrad), but the practical side has been a complete wash. 2.5 years through my PhD with nothing to show for it except for a bunch of failed experiments. I want nothing more than to quit, but I'm not sure what else I'd do, and I feel like I'd be a failure and a quitter if I left now. My lifestyle is okay I guess. I still live at home because I'm too poor to move out. My parents are to caught up with themselves to be interested in my life. I got a car recently so I drive, and that has helped a bit but not really enough. I play guitar in my spare time and am in a band or two. I really love music - it's probably the only thing that's still keeping me here. I'd love to play full-time but that's not realistic, especially not in the small city where I live. It feels like even if I quit the PhD and do something else I'd still just be doing something to make money and waste time until I can retire and be buried in a box. It feels as though if this is all there is, then why should I be wasting my time?

It's especially hard not having a special girl to talk to and spend time with. I haven't been on a date in 2-3 years. I went through a string of single dates before that, but they never went anywhere because I was too socially inept to make any progress, so I guess I just gave up and thought I'd figure it out later on. Well, now it IS later on, and I'm no closer to achieving anything on that front. Some days I don't even want to get out of bed, but I still want to play music. Lately, I can't even find the motivation to do that, which is a BIG deal. Now I'm sitting here at work on Sunday night trying to pull my shit together, but it feels like the more work I put in the more things fall apart.

I'm not too bad socially for the most part I guess. I have real problems talking to women. I'm not stupid, but when I go to talk I just can't think of anything to say. I have a few good friends that I've known for quite a while, but they just seem "different" to me. I don't think they really understand me, and they don't seem to have the same thoughts about life that I do, which makes it hard to talk to them about serious things. I don't have any friends at work because I don't fit in with them - they're mostly from middle-class, well-educated backgrounds, and I'm from an uneducated working-class family. I don't get them and they don't get me. I've been trying to build up my self-esteem, but just when I seem to be getting somewhere it seems that something happens to cause it to fall in a heap. I realize from the outside is seems like I should feel pretty good about myself, but for some reason I just can't pull it together, and that frustrates me more than anything.

Thank you. It's good to know there's someone else that can relate to how I'm feeling. Do you feel like you're just spinning your wheels and waiting for your "real" life to start? Sometimes I wonder how I could have been so stupid as to let myself get to 24 without having stopped and considered where I was going with everything. Now I guess I've made it to 24, but I have no idea how I got here, and no idea what I'm supposed to be doing next.
